title: Privilege Fuseboard and Operational Guardrails: RBAC v2 Role Model Draft
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a pragmatic RBAC v2 role model that balances least-privilege defaults with operational safety for admins and platform teams. This ticket captures a single-source draft for: (1) resource hierarchy and scope resolution, (2) canonical permission atoms and permission matrix, (3) inheritance and deny/allow semantics, (4) audit-event schema mapping, and (5) SSO/SAML attribute & group-to-role mapping recommendations.

Key constraints:
- Must support multi-tenant isolation (org, project, environment) and Dedicated/Private deployment modes.
- Low-latency permission checks (cacheable decisions) while retaining auditability.
- Clear admin guardrails: breakglass, temporal elevation, constrained impersonation, and strong audit trails.

Deliverables:
- Permission matrix CSV (flat atoms) for platform, runtime, console, and billing surfaces.
- Scope resolution algorithm and examples.
- Admin operations playbook (how to safely perform emergency escalations).
- Integration checklist for SSO/SAML/SCIM provisioning and audit mapping.

Non-goals: Model does not cover per-prompt content moderation policies or ML model weight access control (will be separate doc).
decisions: Adopt a three-tier resource hierarchy: organization > workspace (logical project) > resource (model/deployment/route). Workspaces are first-class tenants for billing and policy scoping.
Define permission atoms as verbs on resource classes (e.g., deployment.read, deployment.write, deployment.invoke, route.override, billing.view). Keep atoms small and composable.
Default policy: deny-by-default. Explicit allows are required for any action; we will support explicit deny for emergency/temporal blocks which override allows.

Inheritance: allows cascade down the hierarchy (org -> workspace -> resource) unless shadowed by an explicit deny at a lower level. Deny precedence: an explicit deny at any level wins over any allow inherited from ancestors.

Admin roles are composition of capability groups rather than single monolithic "superadmin". Provide two guarded paths for full control: (a) Breakglass with logged justification + audit retention, (b) Time-limited elevation using short-lived tokens tied to an approver flow.

Audit events must include: actor_id, principal_source (SAML/SCIM/local), effective_permissions_snapshot, resource_path, decision_reason (inheritance/explicit-allow/explicit-deny), session_id, ip, timestamp, and obfuscated_request_payload when needed for PII-sensitive ops.

SSO mapping: prefer SCIM group-to-role assignments for deterministic provisioning. For SAML, map attributes (eduPersonPrincipalName or group assertions) into workspace-scoped role assignments. Support attribute-based rules for environment-specific role bindings (e.g., group:infra-prod -> workspace:prod -> role:deploy).

Cache strategy: cache effective permission tuples per subject per workspace for up to 5 minutes; invalidate on role-binding or group-sync events. Cache must store justification version id to surface stale checks in audits.

Fail-open vs fail-closed: for API request authorization the system must fail-closed on internal errors. For read-only console views, degrade to informational mode with a prominent warning if authz backend is unavailable.
Compatibility: expose an evaluation API that returns (allowed: boolean, reasons: [strings], effective_permissions: [atoms]) to aid debugging and operator tooling.
Migration: provide an automated importer that maps current RBAC v1 buckets into candidate role templates with a dry-run mode and a verification audit log before commit.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Zoe Kim: Ran tabletop exercises with oncall to validate breakglass flow. Found two gaps: (1) missing short-circuit logging for rollback actions, (2) lack of ephemeral token revocation endpoint. Added to decisions.

2026-02-24 - Asha Patel: Security review kickoff scheduled. Draft audit schema attached to ticket for feedback (link: confluence/redwood/security/rbac-audit-schema).

2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Prototype of scope resolution algorithm implemented in the authz-sim service (PR: github.com/redwood/authz-sim#124). Tests include multi-group and workspace-scoped lookups. Performance baseline: avg 1.8ms per check with local cache warmed.
2026-03-08 - Priya Desai (security): Approved core audit fields but requested encryption-at-rest for audit logs and retention policy proposal. Added acceptance criteria item.
acceptance_criteria: Permission matrix published and reviewed by product, security, and platform teams.
Scope resolution algorithm documented with 8 example scenarios (org-level allow, workspace explicit deny, overlapping group bindings, temporal elevation).
Authz evaluation API implemented with comprehensive unit tests and 90%+ coverage for decision reasons paths.
Audit event schema implemented in the logging pipeline with encrypted storage and retention policy defined.
SSO/SCIM mappings documented with a migration runbook and at least one customer demo using SCIM group sync.
Security sign-off recorded and a follow-up ticket created for operational rollout automation (ENG-26390).
notes: This design intentionally separates 'permission atoms' from 'roles' to make role composition auditable and to reduce lateral privilege grants. We will supply a reference UI in the console that shows the effective permission set per principal to assist audits.
